merger_name: Royal Caribbean Cruises – Sandals Resorts International

anzsic_codes.name: Travel Agency and Tour Arrangement Services

merger_description:
The Proposed Transaction will be effected by Bracknell S. de R.L. (**Atlas JVCo**), a special purpose vehicle established for the purpose of the Acquisition.

Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. (**RCL**) is proposing to enter agreements with Sandals Resorts International 2000, Inc. and Hospitality Purveyors, Inc. (Panama) (together, **Sandals Resorts**) and Majerem Limited under which RCL (through Atlas JVCo) will acquire a 50% interest in the combined hotel business operations and sales and marketing operations comprising the Sandals Resorts business (the **Acquisition**).

RCL is a global cruise and vacation company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange, that provides ocean cruise holidays and cruise-related holiday experiences. It operates 71 ships through its three wholly owned brands, Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea, and a 50% joint venture interest in TUI Cruises, which operates the Mein Schiff and Hapag-Lloyd brands.

Through its wholly owned brands and joint ventures, RCL offers contemporary, premium and luxury cruise holidays, including onboard accommodation, dining, entertainment and recreational activities, as well as access to ports and private holiday destinations around the world.

Sandals Resorts owns and operates all-inclusive luxury resorts and associated hospitality services in the Caribbean. Its brand portfolio consists of Sandals Resorts, its luxury adults-oriented resorts that provide premium accommodation, dining, beverages, recreation and entertainment. Sandals Resorts also operates Beaches Resorts, its all-inclusive family resort brand which provides family-focussed, all-inclusive holidays, including accommodation, dining, children’s programs, waterparks, entertainment and other recreational activities.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise any material lessening of
competition given there is no horizontal overlap or vertical
relationship between RCL and Sandals Resorts in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
